T000001974097.title: [Elis SA, Q1 2020 Sales/ Trading Statement Call, Apr 28, 2020](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$DOCID_T000001974097)

text: For the one-off COVID-related over cost. [#414](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002049748-414)
In many cases, we had the project before COVID crisis from SID to accelerate. [#157](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002049748-157)

In Healthcare, we have been able to sign some new business, for example, with some small hospitals that switch to the outsourcing business model during the crisis, but this was offset by the fact that most countries have decided to postpone all non-urgent medical treatments to make more room for COVID-19 patients, often resulting in some hospitals being partially empty, which means lower activity for us. [#53](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000001974097-53)

The COVID-19 crisis obviously had a very material impact on our top line, with organic revenue down minus 15% in H1 and minus 27% in Q2. [#16](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002049748-16)

It's made up, first, one-off at the peak of the COVID crisis in Q2 for EUR 22 million, just as bonus for , additional protective equipment for employees and so on; second, restructuring costs linked to redundancy plans and closure of plants for EUR 33 million; and third, EUR 5 million of acquisition costs. [#221](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002232515-221)

In Healthcare, the measures aiming at saving some rooms for COVID-19 patients that we already mentioned a few times today has been intensifying in April, leading to a circa minus 15% organic decrease year-on-year. [#175](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000001974097-175)

So if we are going to expect a waiver for 2020, the December, would that sort of cut out the dividend for 2020 and possibly put a limit on M&A? [#299](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000001974097-299)

The main items [ reflected ] between net result and headline net result are the same as usual: PPA depreciation, noncash IFRS 2 expense for the [ 3-year ] plan and major one-off net of tax which are [ busier ] restructuring costs and COVID-19 incremental costs. [#231](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002232515-231)
You have seen also that we have been able to manage our cost basis during the peak of the crisis in Brazil. [#449](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002232515-449)
So do you expect this number of loss ratio to be worse in the next months because of the crisis? [#211](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000001974097-211)
So we were quite transparent about the fact that, well, to improve liquidity, it's a good idea to cut dividend. [#350](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000001974097-350)

In Healthcare, we also noted a gradual decrease in volumes for Q1 as the NHS has been rolling out a massive plan to postpone non-urgent treatments to make more room available for COVID-19 patients. [#88](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000001974097-88)
We have -- I think we have demonstrated that the concept of fixed or flexible cost is depending on the magnitude of the crisis. [#402](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000001974097-402)

Our available liquidity today stands at EUR 1.1 billion, and we kept working on further improving it, notably through the cancellation of the dividend and the temporary suspension of our M&A activity. [#34](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000001974097-34)
And the business is profitable enough to digest such a crisis. [#502](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002232515-502)
